content:
James Gunn and Peter Safran are stepping down as the heads of DC Studios, ending a four-year run in charge of Warner Bros.' DC film and television universe. Marvel Studios veteran Jeremy Latcham will take over as president and chief creative officer, effective December 1, 2026.

The shake-up was first reported by Variety on Monday, November 9, and confirmed by The Hollywood Reporter, Deadline, and USA Today. Gunn confirmed the news himself in a statement posted to Threads, writing that running the studio had been "trying, to say the least," and saying he was relieved to return to pure filmmaking.

A surprise exit after the Skydance takeover

The timing caught Hollywood off guard. Gunn and Safran had been named to David Ellison's leadership team at the newly renamed Skydance after Paramount's $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery closed in October 2026. The merger was completed on October 6.

Skydance chair and CEO David Ellison and co-CEO Ynon Kreiz framed the change as a transition following the acquisition. Whether Gunn and Safran chose to step back or were pushed out remains an open question in the coverage; the companies' statements present a collaborative handover, and Gunn and Safran will continue working with DC during the transition.

In a joint statement to Variety, Gunn and Safran said: "Four years ago, we set out to unite DC under one creative vision." They added that they were "immensely proud" of the team behind the new DC Universe and said they were eager to see the perspective Latcham brings to the studio's next chapter.

What Gunn and Safran built

Gunn and Safran were appointed in 2022 to rebuild DC's film and television strategy as one connected universe. Under their leadership, the studio released Superman in 2025, restoring the Man of Steel to the center of the franchise, along with the television series Peacemaker and Creature Commandos, and the upcoming series Lanterns and the film Clayface.

Variety described the duo's tenure as a reset of DC's comic book division with mixed commercial results, but the Superman relaunch gave the new universe a solid foundation and a clear creative direction.

Who is Jeremy Latcham?

Latcham is a Marvel veteran who joined Marvel Studios in 2004 and worked closely with president Kevin Feige during the early development of the Marvel Cinematic Universe. His credits include Guardians of the Galaxy, Avengers, and Spider-Man films. He worked directly with Gunn on Guardians of the Galaxy.

As president and chief creative officer, Latcham will lead DC's film, television, and animation slate, overseeing the creative pipeline, production, talent, and strategy. He will report to Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein, co-chairs of Skydance Motion Picture Group.

What happens next for DC fans

Gunn and Safran are not leaving DC altogether. Gunn remains writer and director of Man of Tomorrow, the Superman sequel due next summer, and he said he has been engaged on another DC project he is writing. Both will continue as producers on DC projects, including The Batman: Part II, starring Robert Pattinson, which is listed for February 2028.

For fans in Laredo and the 956, the change means the DC Universe's next chapter will be guided by a Marvel veteran who helped build the MCU from the ground up, while the filmmaker behind the new Superman stays on to finish the story he started. The slate Latcham inherits is already set through 2028, so the first real test of his vision will come after that.

Sources:

  • Variety — first report of the leadership change, November 9, 2026
  • The Hollywood Reporter — confirmation and details on the transition
  • USA Today — "DC Studios bosses James Gunn, Peter Safran out in stunning shake-up," November 9, 2026
  • Deadline — confirmation and reporting on the Skydance transition
